added_models.model: Syngeneic murine HCC allograft in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice (apatinib monotherapy, NK-dependent; Yang 2020)

efficacy.model: Syngeneic murine HCC allograft in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice (apatinib monotherapy, NK-dependent; Yang 2020)
efficacy.note: Apatinib alone attenuated tumour growth and normalised vessels in a syngeneic immunocompetent HCC mouse; AHELP had not yet reported.
efficacy.short: Syngeneic mouse: apatinib slowed tumours; AHELP unreported
efficacy.quote: Here, using a syngeneic HCC mouse model, we demonstrated that treatment with apatinib resulted in attenuation of tumor growth and increased tumor vessel normalization.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Cancer Gene Therapy, paywalled). The host strain (C57BL/6) is named on the article page; the tumour line is not confirmed from what I read. Manuscript received 2019-12-28, before AHELP's first public readout (ASCO abstract issued 2020-05-20).
efficacy.judgement: Own track: an immunocompetent syngeneic allograft with a murine tumour and intact NK/T cells is a different system from the human cell-line xenografts in immunodeficient rodents the draft pools; the prediction (class activity in HCC) is the same, and the brief makes each system a track. Opens untested at first public use.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic murine HCC allograft in immunocompetent C57BL/6 mice (apatinib monotherapy, NK-dependent; Yang 2020)
efficacy.note: AHELP: apatinib improved OS over placebo in second-line HCC (HR 0.785), matching the syngeneic allograft's prediction of monotherapy activity.
efficacy.short: AHELP OS win matched syngeneic-mouse prediction
efficacy.quote: Overall survival was significantly improved in the apatinib group compared with the placebo group (median 8·7 months [95% CI 7·5‒9·8] vs 6·8 months [5·7‒9·1]; hazard ratio 0·785 [95% CI 0·617‒0·998], p=0·048).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Yang 2020 and Qin 2021. Timing: Yang 2020 was received 2019-12-28 and accepted 2020-05-29; AHELP's primary result first appeared as an ASCO abstract issued 2020-05-20 (Crossref), so the model was run before the result was public and retrodiction is false. The paper's own aim was the anti-PD-1 combination; the monotherapy arm is what is scored.
efficacy.reason: Apatinib shrank syngeneic tumours; AHELP OS met
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the trial paper does not cite the syngeneic model. Same, direction only: apatinib monotherapy attenuated tumour growth in the immunocompetent allograft and AHELP met its OS primary against placebo. Only apatinib has been run in this system, so no other member's miss bears on the track. CARES-310 (camrelizumab plus rivoceranib), the combination this model was built to explain, is recorded, not scored.

patient_trials.quote: Apatinib significantly improved overall survival in patients with pretreated advanced hepatocellular carcinoma compared with placebo, with a manageable safety profile.

Median overall survival was significantly extended with camrelizumab-rivoceranib versus sorafenib (22·1 months [95% CI 19·1-27·2] vs 15·2 months [13·0-18·5]; HR 0·62 [95% CI 0·49-0·80]; one-sided p<0·0001).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: attenuation of tumour growth in syngeneic mice (figure-level, abstract read) vs AHELP OS HR 0.785; not commensurable

added_models.model: Patient-derived liver-cancer stem-cell clones (MEF-feeder culture) supplying a 12-gene prognostic signature; TCGA-LIHC C1/C2 subtypes with axitinib sensitivity imputed in silico (oncoPredict, GDSC-trained)

efficacy.model: Patient-derived liver-cancer stem-cell clones (MEF-feeder culture) supplying a 12-gene prognostic signature; TCGA-LIHC C1/C2 subtypes with axitinib sensitivity imputed in silico (oncoPredict, GDSC-trained)
efficacy.note: LCSC-derived 12-gene signature splits TCGA-LIHC into C1/C2; oncoPredict imputes C2 patients axitinib-sensitive; no patient was treated by subtype.
efficacy.short: C2 subtype imputed axitinib-sensitive; no patients
efficacy.quote: Patients of the C2 subtype, which is closely related to the extracellular matrix, were found to be sensitive to treatments such as Cisplatin, Axitinib, JAK1 inhibitors, WNT-c59, Sorafenib, and RO-3306.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (Europe PMC, open access). The axitinib call is an oncoPredict ridge-regression imputation on TCGA-LIHC transcriptomes trained on GDSC cell-line IC50s, stratified by a consensus-cluster subtype built on 12 LCSC-high prognostic genes; sixteen LCSC strains were isolated from 24 tissues and ten were tumorigenic in mice, but no clone and no patient was exposed to axitinib.
efficacy.reason: No patient dosed by LCSC subtype
efficacy.judgement: Own track rather than the draft's hcc-patient-derived-primary-cell-lines: different model (stem-cell clones on MEF feeders plus a GDSC-trained imputation, versus mouse-passaged primary lines exposed to the drug in vitro) and different prediction (a transcriptomic subtype class, versus a per-donor responder ranking). model_kind in_silico because the axitinib sensitivity was computed, not measured; the checker's 'patient-derived LCSC line' framing describes the signature's source, not the drug test. Untested, not blank: the model exists, names a member drug, and nobody compared it with treated patients.
efficacy.population: Unselected (TCGA-LIHC transcriptomes stratified by LCSC-gene subtype; C2 = extracellular-matrix-high)

considered_not_added: Liang 2019 Exp Mol Med (the checker's 'Lu 2019'; first author is Liang Q; doi 10.1038/s12276-019-0274-7, PMID 31285418, epub 2019-07-08): HepG2-Red-fLuc and SMMC-7721-fLuc subcutaneous plus HepG2 orthotopic xenografts in athymic BALB/c nude mice on apatinib vs sorafenib; tail-cuff mean blood pressure rose on day 10 (69.5 vs 62.3 mmHg control), urine creatinine and protein and serum ALT/AST rose. This is the same human cell-line xenograft in nude mice that the draft's hcc-human-xenograft-immunodeficient-rodent track already pools (Yang 2018 apatinib mouse xenografts), so it is not a new track: it is a safety-cell addition on that existing track (product_in_model true, published before AHELP's 2020-05-20 ASCO readout) and the model_src that would make the draft's safety entry 4 product_in_model true.
McNamara 2015 DCE-US (doi 10.1002/cncr.29227): patient-side evidence for the existing xenograft track's engagement cell (the checker's correction to downstream same, 2015), not a model system.

Tivozanib first-in-human PD (AV-951-03-B01: dose-dependent serum sVEGFR-2 fall and tumour-perfusion reduction, FDA 212904 Multidiscipline Review lines 1417-1420; Eskens 2011): patient-side, other-indication solid tumours, for the existing xenograft track's engagement cell; admissibility is the checker's rule question 1.

FDA 212904 rat-vs-clinical exposure statement (rat 0.2 mg/kg Cmax 70-108 ng/mL, AUC 1640 ng*h/mL vs 86.9 ng/mL and 1510 ng*h/mL at 1.34 mg/day): patient-side, comparison stated by the regulator, for the existing xenograft track's dose cell (checker's correction to same, 2021).

Zhuo 2021 Cell Death Dis (doi 10.1038/s41419-021-04320-4, PMID 34785656): CK19+/- HCC cells isolated from patients; apatinib was an in-vitro comparator and did not preferentially inhibit CK19+ cells, the PDX arm (10 patients) ran regorafenib only (outside the member list), and the patient comparison is CK19 status vs recurrence after transplantation, not response to any member drug. No apatinib patient comparison; a null patient-level prediction for apatinib. Could be an untested patient-level track under decision 8 if wanted; not added.

Cui 2025 Sci Rep (doi 10.1038/s41598-025-32228-y, PMID 41398194): Hepa1-6 syngeneic mice, apatinib plus PD-1 inhibitor; the same syngeneic system as the added track but a combination mechanism study published after CARES-310 (2023). Combination trials are recorded, not scored, on this tile; changes no status.

Huang 2026 Front Immunol (doi 10.3389/fimmu.2026.1617227, PMID 41782865): QSP virtual-cohort model of camrelizumab plus apatinib predicting that 125 mg apatinib matches the original dose and naming CD8+/Treg, CD4+/Treg and MDSC density as biomarkers. In silico for the combination, built after CARES-310; its dose and biomarker predictions have not been tested in patients and no trial used it to choose a dose, so it has not been compared with patients.
Prognostic nomograms for TACE plus apatinib (BMC Gastroenterol 2024, PMID 38589828): statistical patient-side models, not a preclinical system.

Apatinib-resistance mouse work (Akkermansia muciniphila, Transl Cancer Res 2026, PMID 42724514) and the AST-3424 prodrug combination (J Pharmacol Sci 2023, PMID 37169481): apatinib as resistance or combination context, no member-drug prediction compared with patients.

HCC organoids, PDX, zebrafish xenografts, precision-cut slices, humanized mice: no study of apatinib, axitinib or tivozanib in any of these found in Europe PMC (title or abstract); the organoid biobanks on the sibling multikinase tile tested sorafenib, lenvatinib or regorafenib, outside this member list.
